quote.text: In the absence of the gold standard, there is no way to protect savings from confiscation through inflation.
quote.author: Alan Greenspan, "Gold and Economic Freedom" (1966)

macro.title: What It Means for VWRA, Global Bonds, Gold & BTC

stories.headline: The Strikes Move Inland, and Iran Answers Across Four Borders in a Night
stories.dek: A second American round in three days hit Iran's southern coast — and a home in Sirik where a wedding was under way. Overnight, Iranian missiles fell on bases in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait and northern Iraq. Brent jumped five per cent to ninety-five dollars, and no capital has drawn the off-ramp.

stories.headline: Nvidia Reportedly Bids Up to Fourteen Billion for the Hub Everyone Downloads From
stories.dek: The figure has risen from thirteen billion to about fourteen in a week, with a reported billion just to keep the staff — and still no signature. Owning Hugging Face would let Nvidia hold the neutral shelf that every rival's chips reach for their models.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · The Undercurrent — Vietnam
stories.headline: The People's Gold Goes Digital
stories.dek: Hanoi has finally torn down its gold monopoly and dreams of drawing the nation's five hundred tonnes of private gold into the banks. At the same moment, a generation is doing the opposite — putting more away, gram by gram, on payday, through apps and a sixty-five-thousand-member Facebook group. The state keeps asking for its gold back. The young have already answered.

stories.headline: A Stablecoin You Can Trust Pays You Nothing — and Is Backed to the Last Cent
stories.dek: MAS opened its draft law on 1 September: a regulated stablecoin must hold one dollar of high-quality reserves for every token, redeem at par, and pay no interest. It is a bet that the way to make private money trustworthy is to strip out the yield that makes it tempting.

stories.headline: The Grail Towel Is the Wrong Towel for a Singapore Bathroom
stories.dek: A towel is decided by the length of the cotton fibre, not the weight of the pile — and in a humid bathroom the plush seven-hundred-gram trophy is the one that goes sour. Buy the long-staple mid-weight that dries by evening, and let the grail stay in the showroom.

stories.kicker: The Home Lab · What Actually Fits
stories.headline: Two Trillion-Class Models Dropped in a Day. The One That Runs Is the Small One.
stories.dek: On 28 August the open-weight headlines were two giants that fit no desk. The story for a single graphics card is quieter and older by two weeks — a twenty-seven-billion-parameter model that lands in seventeen gigabytes and answers at reading speed.

stories.headline: The Glasses Whose Whole Pitch Is What They Left Out
stories.dek: RayNeo's iO ships tomorrow at four hundred and seventy-nine dollars — no camera, no speaker, just a monochrome display only the wearer can see. It undercuts the reader's own Even Realities G2 by a hundred and twenty, and answers the question everyone asks the Meta glasses: is that thing filming me?

stories.headline: Omega Brings Back the Speedmaster a Generation Started On
stories.dek: The redesigned 38-millimetre Speedmaster ditches the oval subdials everyone quietly hated and puts a Co-Axial chronometer movement in an automatic chronograph from sixty-five hundred dollars — the spiritual heir to the old Reduced, and this time the reviews have actually landed.

stories.headline: Danny Boyle Opens Venice With the Making of a Tabloid
stories.dek: "Ink" dramatises Rupert Murdoch's 1969 purchase of The Sun and the editor who remade it into Britain's best-seller. The premiere drew a five-minute standing ovation and the year's first "masterpiece" — and a montage that runs the line straight from 1969 to Trump and Musk.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Phone Question
stories.headline: The Year the Rules Around Her Phone Were Redrawn
stories.dek: She starts Secondary 1 in a school where phones are locked away all day, and turns 13 into platforms being forced to check her age. The research says the lever that matters most may not be whether she has an account, but how old she is when she starts.

stories.headline: Everything Falls but Oil and the Dollar
stories.dek: A Strait of Hormuz supply shock became an inflation scare, and money markets flipped from pricing a September cut to leaning toward a hike. The sharpest tell: gold at a multi-week low in the middle of a Middle East war.

stories.headline: The Reel Is the Part You Take Away
stories.dek: A long telescopic rod, a line tied straight to the tip, one fly, no reel. Tenkara is the Japanese mountain-stream method that strips fly fishing back to a hand, a line and a fish — a whole hobby built on subtraction, and one that quietly grows a quiver anyway.

stories.headline: Grip Strength Predicts How Long You Live — but It Is a Marker, Not a Lever
stories.dek: A new study ties a firm handshake and a fast chair-rise to a third lower death risk. The catch is the one the honest reader should hold onto: the strength is the signal that you are robust, not the switch that makes you so.

stories.headline: A Padang Full of Headliners, and a Fukuoka Basho to Book the Flights Around
stories.dek: The Grand Prix brings the strongest concert bill the Padang has carried — Lana Del Rey's first Singapore show among them — and Japan's autumn stacks a sold-out Tokyo basho, an Orsay blockbuster and the last of the leaves.
